indicator_name: Proportion of people saying they felt loneliness “a lot of the day yesterday”
area_description: Social cohesion underpins informal safety nets, collective action and public support for redistributive and welfare policies. Social isolation is linked to poor mental and physical health across  income levels. Social cohesion is often underrepresented in other frameworks but is increasingly relevant as isolation and  loneliness are on the rise in many societies.
source_organisation_1: German Institute for Economic Research
source_url_text_1: Loneliness in Germany – prevalence, trends over time and regional differences (only available in German)

graph_title: People who felt loneliness “a lot of the day yesterday”
footnotes:
The proportion of people who reported having felt lonely ‘for most of yesterday’ is a Gallup World Poll indicator. It forms part of the measurement of subjective well-being and negative emotions.
  • Definition: People who answered ‘often’ or ‘very often’ to all three items on the UCLA-3 Loneliness Scale are considered to be ‘highly lonely’. The figures relate to adults aged 18 and over in Germany who live in private households.
